import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_33/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_33/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_33/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source3_33_2 and Source3_33_0 on movie_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source0[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the result with Source3_33_1 on user_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source1[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema and ensure correct types
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Convert movie_id to int (from source it is int, but after merge it might be float)
join_2['movie_id'] = join_2['movie_id'].astype(int)

# Ensure user_id, rating, timestamp, age, occupation are float
join_2['user_id'] = join_2['user_id'].astype(float)
join_2['rating'] = join_2['rating'].astype(float)
join_2['timestamp'] = join_2['timestamp'].astype(float)
join_2['age'] = join_2['age'].astype(float)
join_2['occupation'] = join_2['occupation'].astype(float)

# Select and reorder columns exactly as target schema
Target3_33 = join_2[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Save the final target table to the specified path
Target3_33.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_33_2 and Source3_33_0 on movie_id
joined_1 = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_33_1 on user_id
joined_2 = pd.merge(joined_1, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that are unique identifiers:
# title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate mean for rating, timestamp, age, occupation (all float columns)
grouped = joined_2.groupby(["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write output to the specified path
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
